sections.html:
Centerton sits in Benton County on Arkansas Highway 102, roughly 5 miles west of Bentonville, the county seat. Highway 102 is the road most residents use to cross town, and Northwest Arkansas Regional Airport lies just south of the city limits. Buyers shopping here usually start with one question: how long is the drive to Bentonville?

The place has changed fast. Census counts went from 2,146 people in 2000 to 17,792 in 2020, and the 2025 estimate is 27,176. In 2020 there were 6,280 housing units, and 5.6% of them stood empty. Centerton works as a Bentonville suburb, so many of its buyers come from the regional job base (Walmart, Tyson Foods, J.B. Hunt) or are relocating into the area.

Rapid growth means a lot of newer houses nearby. If yours is older, expect buyers to compare it against fresh construction, so condition and price carry extra weight.

Bentonville School District covers most of Centerton. A small slice of the west side belongs to the Decatur School District. Bentonville West High School is inside the city. Elementary zoning varies, with Centerton Gamble Elementary serving much of town and other areas assigned elsewhere. Zones change from street to street, so look up your own address with the district before you tell a buyer where the kids would go.

The Building Safety department handles building, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, demolition, pool and solar permits and reviews plans. You schedule inspections through the online portal at bsaonline.com. Fire inspections run through the Fire Marshal or Fire Chief instead. A certificate of occupancy comes before anyone moves into a structure, so it matters mostly for new or newly finished construction.

For older work or an open permit, email buildingsafety@centertonar.us or call 479-795-2750.

Walk through the property with this short list before you put it on the market:

  • Does the deck, shed, pool or addition have a permit on file?
  • Is any permit still waiting on a final inspection?
  • Do your subdivision covenants restrict changes you have made?

Lenders and inspectors tend to catch unpermitted work, and it can derail a closing late in the process. Fixing it first leaves you with more options.

Benton County rests on the Springfield Plateau, a limestone region with springs, sinkholes and caves. Centerton itself grew up around a spring. So expect buyers to ask where water goes when it rains, and be ready to say. Roofs after a storm and heating systems after a cold snap draw questions as well. Pull together receipts and dates now, before the first showing.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Benton County's collector sends the bill. The books open the first business day of March. Anything still unpaid after October 15 gets a 10 percent penalty, and unpaid real estate also builds interest. Tax statements go out by July 1.

Arkansas bills a year behind. A 2026 assessment turns into a bill in 2027, due October 15, 2027. The owner of record on January 1 of the tax year receives the bill. Your closing paperwork shows how the buyer and seller divide the current year. When a mortgage company pays the tax from escrow, confirm within 30 to 60 days that the payment actually went through.

sections.h2: What a sale does to your assessment
sections.html:
After title transfers, the Benton County assessor reappraises the house at 20 percent of appraised value on the next assessment date. The new owner loses the assessed-value limitation until the second assessment date following the transfer. A primary residence qualifies for a homestead credit of up to $600. The next countywide reappraisal is set for 2028.

The state also collects a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration, on transfers above $100. The state's transfer tax page explains how it works.

An unpaid bill does not stop a sale, but it follows the property. Late tax carries the 10 percent penalty and interest, so the amount grows the longer it sits. Ask the Benton County collector for a current balance before you accept any offer. The title company will find the debt anyway and pay it out of your proceeds at closing, so you want that number in hand when you compare offers.

If a mortgage servicer pays your tax through escrow, look at the escrow statement instead. A missed payment there is easy to overlook, and it is worth sorting out before a buyer's title search turns it up.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
Whatever route you choose, the order is similar. First, collect the paperwork: the latest tax statement, any permit records for additions, and a payoff figure from your mortgage company. Second, decide how fast you need to close, since that drives whether a listing or a direct sale makes sense. Third, get offers in writing and compare what you would actually receive after repairs, fees and carrying costs. Fourth, the title company opens an order, checks ownership and liens, and sets the closing date. At closing the tax proration, any payoff and the transfer tax are settled on one statement, and you hand over the keys.

A cash purchase skips the buyer's loan appraisal and the lender's repair list, so those two common delays do not apply.

sections.h2: What to have ready for the title company
sections.html:
• Your most recent tax statement and proof of payment for earlier years.
  • Permit records for any addition, deck, pool or outbuilding.
  • A mortgage payoff letter, if you still owe on the loan.
  • Names of everyone on the deed, since each owner of record must sign.
  • Receipts for recent roof, heating or drainage work.

Showing up with these items shortens the title search and gives a buyer fewer reasons to renegotiate. It also lets you judge a cash offer against a listing using real figures instead of guesses.

Typical sellers here own a newer house in a busy area, are relocating, inherited a property, or run a rental. Some have a house that needs repairs a conventional lender would demand before funding a loan.

A cash offer takes the lender out of the picture, so approval and appraisal stop being obstacles. Weigh it against a listing on speed and on the amount you would walk away with, and insist on seeing the offer in writing.

Inherited houses and rentals add one more step. With an inherited property, make sure whoever signs actually holds title. With a rental, tell any buyer early about the tenant, because an occupied house limits what a buyer can do with it and can change both price and timing.

faqs.a: Centerton is in Benton County, about 5 miles west of Bentonville on Arkansas Highway 102. Decatur is 11 miles farther west.

faqs.q: What school district is Centerton in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Bentonville School District, with a small western part in the Decatur School District. Bentonville West High School is in Centerton.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Centerton?
faqs.a: Payment is due by October 15, and a 10 percent penalty follows. The collector opens the books on the first business day of March.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate of occupancy to sell my Centerton house?
faqs.a: The certificate is issued before a structure is occupied, so it mainly applies to new or newly finished construction. Call Building Safety at 479-795-2750 about older work or open permits.

faqs.q: Does the sale change my assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. After title transfers, the Benton County assessor reappraises the house at 20 percent of appraised value on the next assessment date.
